ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: There are two space-filling molecular models in the figure. The model on the left is obviously smaller, and the model on the right is obviously larger; both have the appearance of tetrahedral carbon tetrahalide molecules. Since the bromine atom has a larger radius than the chlorine atom, the larger model on the right corresponds to CBr4, and the smaller model on the left corresponds to CCl4. Reasoning: The problem states that the vapor pressures of the two are compared at the same temperature. The CBr4 molecule is larger, and its electron cloud is more easily polarized, so the London dispersion force is stronger and the intermolecular forces are greater. The stronger the intermolecular forces, the less easily the liquid volatilizes, and the lower the vapor pressure. Therefore, the vapor pressure of CBr4 is lower, and the vapor pressure of CCl4 is higher. Final answer: CCl4 has the higher vapor pressure.

method.method_draft: Read the image first to note that one molecule is much larger; match the larger space-filling model to CBr4 and the smaller to CCl4 using Br vs Cl atomic size.
